subject: a 19th-century American inventor with short dark hair falling over a broad forehead, clean-shaven, serious grey eyes, wearing a plain dark wool suit and waistcoat with a loose white collar, shirtsleeves sometimes rolled up, chemical stains on his hands

panels.01-newsboy: a fifteen-year-old boy in a cap and worn 1860s jacket working in the baggage car of a moving steam train in 1862 Michigan, a small hand printing press, stacks of newspapers, shelves of glass chemical bottles, light through the open sliding door, fields rushing past
panels.02-menlo: a long two-storey white wooden laboratory building with a picket fence beside a railway line in a quiet New Jersey hamlet in 1876, a few workmen in waistcoats carrying crates and instruments inside, early spring trees, wide establishing shot
panels.03-phonograph: {S} leaning over a small hand-cranked brass cylinder machine wrapped in tinfoil on a workbench, speaking into its mouthpiece at night in 1877, a bearded Swiss machinist in an apron and two assistants listening in amazement, oil lamps, tools and wires on the bench
panels.04-lamp: {S} and three assistants in shirtsleeves gathered at night around a single small glowing glass bulb on a laboratory bench at Menlo Park in 1879, watching it closely, a glass vacuum pump, notebooks, rows of bottles on shelves behind, warm glow lighting their faces
panels.05-pearlstreet: a lower Manhattan street at dusk in 1882 with brick buildings and gas lamps, offices glowing with new electric light in their windows, workmen in bowler hats beside a dynamo room seen through an open doorway, horse carriages, crowds looking up
panels.06-kinetoscope: {S} older, with greying hair, standing beside a tall wooden cabinet with a peephole viewer in a West Orange laboratory room in 1891, an assistant with a neat moustache adjusting a strip of film, visitors in long 1890s dresses waiting to look, workshop tools
panels.07-battery: an older {S} with grey hair seated at a long laboratory bench covered with hundreds of small test cells and glass jars around 1901, writing figures in a notebook late at night, chemists in aprons working behind him, electric lamps overhead
panels.08-jubilee: a very old {S} with white hair, in a dark suit, reaching up with two wires to connect an old glass bulb in a wooden two-storey laboratory interior in 1929, an elderly former assistant beside him, distinguished guests in 1920s suits watching quietly, warm golden light
